criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs contains a rule that emits a PolicyViolation naming CHANGELOG.md when the reading's deliverables list it, defaults_applied has id `changelog`, and no change in input.changes has path CHANGELOG.md; its doc comment names the root cause (the default was a rule the producer must remember, with no code comparing the diff to the deliverables).
criteria.evidence: In the diff, `admit_without_secrets` pushes `violation("changelog", Some("CHANGELOG.md"), ...)` when `changelog_required(git, base, reading, &paths)` holds. That calls `reading::changelog_unproduced`, which requires capability `change`, a CHANGELOG.md Modify deliverable, a `changelog` default, and no changed path equal to CHANGELOG.md (a leading ./ is ignored). It also skips the rule when the base marks CHANGELOG.md readonly or exclude. The doc comments on `changelog_required`, the inline rule and `changelog_unproduced` all state the root cause: the default was a rule the producer must remember, and no code compared the diff's file list with the deliverables.

findings.evidence: 'Any status counts as touching the file', so a candidate that deletes CHANGELOG.md passes the changelog rule. This edge case is unlikely, and the verifier would still judge it.

summary: The change fixes the root cause where it starts. Before it, the `changelog` default that `ensure_changelog` adds was enforced only by the final verdict. Now a predicate, `reading::changelog_unproduced`, compares a change reading's deliverables and defaults with the candidate's changed paths. Admission and the producer loop share that one predicate, through `admission::changelog_required`. So a producer is sent back once for a missing CHANGELOG.md, and a candidate still missing it is refused at admission, before the verifier. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core admission` and `cargo test -p athena-core changelog`, and the new tests passed. A docs-only design reading built through `ensure_changelog` is refused. Adding the changelog clears the violation, and study readings and readings without the default are exempt. The run-level tests show the send-back, the refusal before the verifier, and the direct path to the verifier. In the evidence snapshot, both failed jobs' readings had capability change, the changelog default and CHANGELOG.md with action modify, so the rule covers the class and not just one instance. fmt, clippy and test are recorded as passed on CI. Athena's fails-without runs hit compile errors instead of assertion failures. By reading the code, though, test (a) must fail if the rule is removed. Two findings: a minor scope note (the producer send-back and test doubles sit outside the deliverables list, but the request's own proposal calls for them), and a nit about deletion counting as touching the file.
